
## `phax artifact abandon`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact abandon <path>`

Abandons an artifact — a terminal status distinct from Completed, for work dropped without execution. Legal from Draft or Approved (specs) or Draft, Approved, or Stale (plans).

Side effects: moves the file into the artifact's archive/ subdirectory with its frontmatter status key rewritten to Abandoned, deletes its approval record file under docs/plans/approvals/ or docs/specs/approvals/ if it has one, and commits the move and the deletion in a single commit; refuses with exit code 12 if any write-set path already has uncommitted changes.

### Arguments

#### `<path>`

Path to a spec or plan file under docs/specs/ or docs/plans/

### Examples

```
phax artifact abandon docs/plans/2607101056-typescript-7-migration-plan.md
```

## `phax artifact complete`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact complete <path>`

Completes an artifact — a terminal status for work that ran to completion. Legal from Approved (specs) or Approved or Stale (plans).

Side effects: moves the file into the artifact's archive/ subdirectory with its frontmatter status key rewritten to Completed, deletes its approval record file under docs/plans/approvals/ or docs/specs/approvals/ if it has one, and commits the move and the deletion in a single commit; refuses with exit code 12 if any write-set path already has uncommitted changes.

### Arguments

#### `<path>`

Path to a spec or plan file under docs/specs/ or docs/plans/

### Examples

```
phax artifact complete docs/specs/2608091526-artifact-lifecycle-status.md
```

## `phax artifact reopen`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact reopen [--by <arbiter>] <path>`

Reopens an artifact back to Draft, voiding its approval, for when it must be revised before re-approval. Legal from Approved (specs and plans) and from Stale (plans only); a Draft, Completed or Abandoned artifact is refused with exit 12 and nothing is written. Rewrites the frontmatter status key in place and clears the `approved` stamp.

Every reopen names its arbiter, as approve does. `--by machine:<grant>` declares a machine by its grant, a kebab-case slug matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$. `--by operator`, or no --by from a terminal, names the operator as git commits: GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, else the repository's git user.name, never a guessed name. Without a terminal there is no default: reopen refuses with exit 12 unless --by is given, naming `--by operator` and `--by machine:<grant>`. An operator reopen refuses with exit 12 when neither is set. While any live spec or plan sidecar is stamped below its document format's current shape, reopen refuses with exit 12, naming each such sidecar and `phax artifact migrate-documents`. Every refusal comes before anything is written. The reopen commit ends with a `Reopened-By: machine (<grant>)` or `Reopened-By: operator (<name>)` trailer.

Reopening a spec leaves every live plan that names it in source-spec unchanged — its file, frontmatter and approval record file — and names each one with its status. Reopen changes only status and approved, which the fingerprint ignores, so a bound plan still reads fresh.

Side effects: writes the artifact file, deletes its approval record file (docs/specs/approvals/<spec file name>.json or docs/plans/approvals/<plan file name>.json) if it has one, and commits them with its JSON document sidecar when headless-authored in a single commit; refuses with exit code 12 if any write-set path already has uncommitted changes.

### Arguments

#### `<path>`

Path to a spec or plan file under docs/specs/ or docs/plans/

### Flags

#### `--by <arbiter>`

operator or machine:<grant>; required without a terminal

### Examples

```
phax artifact reopen docs/plans/2607101056-typescript-7-migration-plan.md --by operator
```

```
phax artifact reopen docs/specs/2609030749-spec-approval-ground.md --by machine:roadmap-loop
```

## `phax artifact decide`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact decide [FLAGS] <path>`

Decides a Draft spec's or plan's open questions in one of two modes: with the operator in an interactive Claude Code session (the default), or from a verdicts file with --verdicts (below).

In interactive mode the session first raises the framing questions F1–F5, then presents the open questions in document order; --question <id> presents that question alone, an open one or an arbitrated one to re-arbitrate (its previous verdict is kept in its history). The session follows the doctrine skill for the artifact's kind (phax-decide-spec or phax-decide-plan; a project copy under .claude/skills/ replaces the bundled one), with --doctrine <file> appended after it; a verdict may cite only the backticked ids that open list items in that doctrine. It resumes the artifact's headless authoring session when phax kept its id, and starts a new one otherwise, and says which.

Interactive decide runs on Claude Code only: the model is --model and --effort, else claude-opus-5-5 at high; a model outside the Claude Code catalog, or an effort it does not list, is refused. When the operator exits the session, phax resumes it headless for the revised document — the whole sidecar document of a headless artifact, `$schema` first at its current shape, or its kind's hand decision answer (spec-hand-decision-answer or plan-hand-decision-answer) for a hand-authored one — and asks once more when the answer is refused. phax stamps each verdict with the committing git identity and the time, checks the answer (only presented questions move, others stay as they were, chosen and abandoned name the question's options or the reserved `other`, cited principles are loaded ids, a departing verdict names what it revised), shows the body diff and the verdicts, and writes nothing unless the operator accepts the diff.

Before any session it refuses, writing nothing: a live sidecar not yet migrated (`phax artifact migrate-documents`), an artifact that is not Draft (an Approved or Stale one names `phax artifact reopen <path>`), a diverged or invalid sidecar, a hand-authored §9 that does not parse (naming its first departing line), uncommitted changes on the artifact or its sidecar, an unknown --question (naming the artifact's question ids), no terminal (interactive mode needs one), a model outside Claude Code (interactive mode), a doctrine file that is unreadable, defines no principle id or redefines a skill id, and no committing git identity. With no open question and no --question it says there is nothing to decide and exits 0. Inside a phase worktree the phase guard refuses it.

Exit codes: 0 decided and committed, a declined diff, or nothing to decide; 1 inside a phase worktree; 5 no document, not JSON, an answer not stamped with its current shape, or one refused by the schema or its checks (after the one corrective resume), or a failed agent session, with nothing written; 8 a provider rate or usage limit, with nothing written; 14 the provider unreachable (a network failure), with nothing written; 12 an artifact refusal, the artifact changed during the session (its change left in place), or a failed commit (the files left written but uncommitted).

Verdicts mode: --verdicts <file|-> reads decisions a person has already made, from a file or from a pipe on stdin (-; a terminal on stdin is refused), and writes them into the artifact without a prompt. The file is JSON with a `$schema` naming the decide-verdicts format of this release (`phax artifact schema verdicts` prints it), an `artifact` key naming the artifact's repo-relative path, and a non-empty `verdicts` list of { question, chosen, note }: `chosen` is one of the question's option ids or the reserved id `other`, and `note` is the person's reason, a non-empty string or null. A note is required when the verdict departs from the recommendation, `other` included; a null note on a question with an empty rationale is refused, since nothing would stand as its why. Every key is required and unknown keys are refused. Questions the file does not name stay open; an arbitrated question it names is re-arbitrated. No terminal is needed with --by operator, which names the operator as git commits; any other --by, machine:<grant> included, is refused (a verdict always comes from the operator), and without --by a terminal is required. One headless writer session, running under the same doctrine, writes the verdicts into the revised document and revises the body where a departing verdict implies it. It runs on the model --model and --effort name, else claude-sonnet-5-5 at medium, routed to a provider like headless authoring (a model with no equivalent on the selected provider runs as the concrete model routing chose, and the report names it beside the requested one); a model routed to Mistral Vibe is refused before any session, since Vibe ignores read-only: pass --model with a Claude Code or Codex model. It resumes the kept authoring session when that session ran on the same provider in this checkout, and starts a new one otherwise, and says which. phax refuses a bad file before any session, checks the writer's answer against the file (each question's options first, then the question set, each chosen and abandoned option, the history, the revised sections, the body outside them; a following verdict revises nothing, except one restoring the recommendation after a departing verdict: it names the sections it restores when that verdict named revised sections, none when it named none, and either when it records none) and asks once more when the check fails, then sets each verdict's why (the note, else the question's rationale), by and at itself. It writes and commits without asking, leaves the artifact Draft, and prints the report to read before approving: each verdict (chosen, followed or departed with the sections revised, and why), the questions left open, the body diff, the commit and the Draft status. With --json it prints that report as one JSON object on stdout (artifact, status, session, provider, model, requestedModel, effort, verdicts, open, diff, commit, decisionId) and sends progress, warnings and record lines to stderr. The commit subject is as in interactive mode, and its body is followed by the trailers Artifact, Decided-By, Decided-Via: verdicts and Decision-Id; the decision record has mode verdicts. --question is refused with --verdicts, and --json and --by are refused without it, exit 12. The exit codes are 0 decided and committed, 1 inside a phase worktree, 5 a refused answer after the one corrective resume or a failed agent session, 8 a provider limit, 12 a refusal, 14 the provider unreachable (a network failure).

Side effects: in interactive mode, spawns an interactive and then a headless Claude Code session, both read-only whatever the security profile (only the Read, Grep and Glob tools, no MCP server), so the session never writes to the repository; keeps the session's prompts, transcripts, answer and diff under the state root's decide/<stamp>-<slug>/<NN>/; on an accepted diff, re-seeds a plan's extraction cache, writes the artifact and its sidecar (or the hand-authored artifact alone) and commits exactly those paths in one commit, with a `Decision-Id: <stamp>-<slug>/<NN>` trailer. Verdicts mode spawns one headless writer session, read-only like the others (which is why a writer model routed to Mistral Vibe, whose adapter ignores read-only, is refused), keeps verdicts.json (the file as given) with the prompts, answer and diff in the same folder, and writes and commits the same paths without a prompt.

### Arguments

#### `<path>`

Path to a spec or plan file under docs/specs/ or docs/plans/

### Flags

#### `--question <id>`

Present this question alone: an open one, or re-arbitrate one

#### `--verdicts <file|->`

Decide from a verdicts file, or - for stdin, without an interactive session

#### `--by <arbiter>`

operator: who gave the verdicts; required without a terminal (with --verdicts)

#### `--json`

Print the report as one JSON object (with --verdicts)

#### `--doctrine <file>`

Append this doctrine file after the decide skill

#### `--model <model>`

Override the decide model (interactive: a Claude Code model)

#### `--effort <effort>`

Override the decide effort

### Examples

```
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md
```

```
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md --question Q1
```

```
phax artifact decide docs/plans/2609261000-plan-prune-store-plan.md --doctrine docs/doctrine/plan.md --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --effort medium
```

```
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md --verdicts verdicts.json --by operator
```

```
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md --verdicts - --by operator --json
```

## `phax artifact new`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact new <SUBCOMMAND>`

Parent command for creating a Draft spec or plan named from the current UTC minute: <YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>.md for a spec, <YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>-plan.md for a plan. The instant is captured when the command runs, never chosen or backdated. A bad slug, an existing target name, or (for a plan) a --spec that is missing or not a spec, a --spec without exactly one of --last/--not-last, or either flag without --spec all refuse with exit code 12 before anything is written.

### Examples

```
phax artifact new spec plan-prune
```

## `phax artifact new spec`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact new spec [FLAGS] <slug>`

Creates a Draft spec at docs/specs/<YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>.md, with a frontmatter-only skeleton (status, date, audience, scope). The slug must match `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`.

Side effects: writes the new spec file. Does not commit — transition commands (phax artifact approve) commit, creation does not.

Pass --headless --brief <file|-> (experimental) to author the spec itself instead of writing a blank skeleton: phax spawns a recorded agent session with the phax-spec skill and the spec document JSON Schema, accepts a schema-valid document as the session's only output, renders it to the canonical Markdown, and writes the rendered spec plus its JSON sidecar. --model and --effort override the resolved authoring model/effort (flag, then phax.json's authoring.spec, then the catalog default). Side effects: spawns a provider session; on success, writes and commits the spec and its sidecar in one commit; nothing lands on a refusal or an invalid session result. When records are configured, every session that ran — committed or failed — writes one authoring record (key authoring/<YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>) on phax/records/v1, and `phax records explain <commit>` resolves it through the artifact commit's Authoring-Id trailer.

### Arguments

#### `<slug>`

Slug matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`

### Flags

#### `--headless`

Author via a recorded agent session from a brief instead of a blank skeleton (experimental)

#### `--brief <file|->`

Path to a brief file, or - to read the brief from stdin

#### `--model <model>`

Override the authoring model (default: flag → config → catalog)

#### `--effort <effort>`

Override the authoring effort (low|medium|high)

### Examples

```
phax artifact new spec plan-prune
```

```
phax artifact new spec plan-prune --headless --brief brief.md
```

## `phax artifact new plan`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact new plan [FLAGS] <slug>`

Creates a Draft plan at docs/plans/<YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>-plan.md, with a frontmatter-only skeleton (status, source-spec, and completes-spec when a spec is bound). Pass --spec <path> to bind an existing spec as the plan's source-spec; the path must classify as a spec (live or archived), exist, and pass artifact validation. With --spec, pass exactly one of --last or --not-last: --last writes completes-spec: true (this plan is the spec's last, and its run completes the spec), --not-last writes completes-spec: false (more plans of the spec follow, and its run leaves the spec live). Every plan of a spec except the last says --not-last; no default is ever inferred. Without --spec, source-spec is written as null with no completes-spec, and both flags are refused. The slug must match `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`.

Side effects: writes the new plan file. Does not commit — transition commands (phax artifact approve) commit, creation does not.

Pass --headless --brief <file|-> (experimental) to author the plan itself instead of writing a blank skeleton: phax spawns a recorded agent session with the phax-planning skill and the plan document JSON Schema (the extracted-plan shape plus informational content), accepts a schema-valid document as the session's only output, renders it to the phax-planning Markdown shape, writes the rendered plan plus its JSON sidecar, and seeds the extraction cache so phax run never re-extracts it. --model and --effort override the resolved authoring model/effort (flag, then phax.json's authoring.plan, then the catalog default). Side effects: spawns a provider session; on success, writes and commits the plan and its sidecar in one commit and seeds the extraction cache; nothing lands on a refusal or an invalid session result. When records are configured, every session that ran — committed or failed — writes one authoring record (key authoring/<YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>) on phax/records/v1, and `phax records explain <commit>` resolves it through the artifact commit's Authoring-Id trailer.

### Arguments

#### `<slug>`

Slug matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`

### Flags

#### `--spec <path>`

Path to the source spec to bind as source-spec

#### `--last`

This plan is its spec's last: its run completes the spec

#### `--not-last`

More plans of the spec follow: its run leaves the spec live

#### `--headless`

Author via a recorded agent session from a brief instead of a blank skeleton (experimental)

#### `--brief <file|->`

Path to a brief file, or - to read the brief from stdin

#### `--model <model>`

Override the authoring model (default: flag → config → catalog)

#### `--effort <effort>`

Override the authoring effort (low|medium|high)

### Examples

```
phax artifact new plan plan-prune-store --spec docs/specs/2609091412-plan-prune.md --not-last
```

```
phax artifact new plan plan-prune-cli --spec docs/specs/2609091412-plan-prune.md --last
```

```
phax artifact new plan catalog-refresh
```

```
phax artifact new plan plan-prune --headless --brief brief.md --spec docs/specs/2609091412-plan-prune.md --last
```

## `phax artifact schema`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact schema <kind>`

Prints the JSON Schema of the experimental spec document (kind spec) or plan document (kind plan), or of a decide verdicts file (kind verdicts, the input of `phax artifact decide --verdicts`), pretty-printed to stdout, so a consumer can read the contract a headless authoring session must satisfy, or the file to write, without a model call.

The spec and plan document formats are experimental: outside the version 1 stability promise, they may change between releases. The printed spec or plan schema is the published answer schema a headless authoring session answers, its `$schema` a const naming the current stamp; the plan document's extracted fields are the extracted-plan shape phax run reads. phax checks, when it decodes a document, what the schema does not express: traceability (every acceptance criterion references existing requirements, every requirement is covered), the question checks (unique question ids, a recommendation among a question's options), the plan's sourceSpec/completesSpec pairing, and an authoring answer's empty arbitratedQuestions.

Side effects: none — read-only.

### Arguments

#### `<kind>`

Document kind: spec, plan or verdicts

### Examples

```
phax artifact schema spec
```

```
phax artifact schema plan
```

```
phax artifact schema verdicts
```

## `phax artifact migrate-approvals`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact migrate-approvals`

Reads docs/plans/approvals.json and docs/specs/approvals.json in any released shape, writes one record file per entry under docs/plans/approvals/ and docs/specs/approvals/, deletes the ledgers, and commits exactly those paths in one commit. Exits 0 when migrated or when there is nothing to migrate; exits 12, writing nothing, on an unreadable ledger, an entry that is not a live artifact path, an uncommitted change to any path it would write, or an existing record file holding a different record.

An entry whose artifact no longer exists still migrates, and is reported on stderr as an orphan record file to delete. An existing record file that already holds the entry's record is kept as is.

Side effects: writes the record files, deletes the ledgers and commits those paths in one commit.

### Examples

```
phax artifact migrate-approvals
```

## `phax artifact migrate-documents`

- **Usage**: `phax artifact migrate-documents`

Rewrites every live spec and plan sidecar (a <name>.json directly under docs/specs/ or docs/plans/ beside its <name>.md) stamped below its document format's current shape, or written before $schema, at that shape, and re-renders its body in the current layout, keeping its frontmatter byte for byte. A spec's questions are lifted by the author's rationale marker: a question whose rationale opens with `Decided by the author on <YYYY-MM-DD>` becomes arbitrated with a lifted, unattributed verdict; every other question stays open. A plan document stamped 0.20.0 lifts with empty preamble questions and keeps its body, lineage and frontmatter as they were. A plan sidecar stamped 0.26.0 or below has each phase's testStrategy string read as test lines: one whose every line follows the line format (`- <guarantee> — <size> · <technique> · <oracle> · <loop>[ · <criterion>]`) is lifted to those lines, and one holding prose is refused, naming the phase, its first departing line and the remedy: rewrite each phase's test strategy in the line format, in the sidecar and plan.md alike, or re-author the plan, then rerun. Archived artifacts, hand-authored artifacts and approval record files are never touched.

Before writing anything it decides everything, and exits 12, writing nothing, on an invalid sidecar (including a plan document stamped 0.17.0–0.19.x, which stays refused), on a plan sidecar whose test strategy is not in the line format, on a body that is not its sidecar's own-shape rendering (a hand edit would be overwritten), or on an uncommitted change to any path it would write; each refused artifact is named with its remedy: re-author it headless, or delete its sidecar to demote it to hand-authored.

The report names each migrated artifact with its status and question counts (open, with their ids, and arbitrated, with how many are lifted), or `body unchanged`. It names every Approved artifact the re-rendering leaves edited since approval — with its open question ids and `phax artifact reopen <path>` when it has any, else `phax artifact approve <path>` — and every live plan it leaves stale with spec-changed evidence. With nothing to migrate it says so, writes nothing and exits 0.

Until it has run, phax artifact approve and phax artifact reopen refuse with exit 12, naming each unmigrated sidecar; complete, abandon and run completion carry an older sidecar as before.

Side effects: writes the sidecars and re-rendered bodies, re-seeds each rewritten plan's extraction cache so phax run never re-extracts it, and commits exactly the rewritten paths in one commit. A failed commit exits 12, leaving the files written but uncommitted.

### Examples

```
phax artifact migrate-documents
```

## `phax plans`

- **Usage**: `phax plans <SUBCOMMAND>`

Parent command for reporting on plans: the mechanical defects of a single plan (lint), a plan laid out phase by phase with its planned files by architecture part, its test lines and the coverage of its source spec's criteria (overview), a plan's API-list cost and its fit in the subscription windows (estimate), staleness of Approved plans against their recorded approval, and cross-plan file overlap.

### Examples

```
phax plans lint docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md
```

```
phax plans overview docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md
```

```
phax plans status
```

```
phax plans overlap docs/plans/2609101031-a-plan.md docs/plans/2609101032-b-plan.md
```

## `phax plans status`

- **Usage**: `phax plans status [--apply] [--json]`

Reports every live, Approved plan's staleness against the ground it was approved against: the declared source spec's content, the plan's own content, and the files changed since the recorded baseline intersected with the plan's footprint. Each stale entry names its reasons (spec-changed, ground-changed, self-changed) with evidence; a plan with no approval record — or one whose baseline commit no longer exists — reports missing-record, which renders as stale. This is a report, not a gate: it exits 0 whether or not stale plans exist. Use --apply to flip stale-computed plans Approved -> Stale as an explicit gesture (the flip is never automatic). Use --json for machine-readable output.

Side effects: read-only unless --apply is set, in which case it writes the flipped plans' frontmatter status key.

### Flags

#### `--apply`

Flip stale-computed plans Approved -> Stale

#### `--json`

Emit the report as JSON instead of a rendered table

### Examples

```
phax plans status
```

```
phax plans status --apply
```

```
phax plans status --json
```

## `phax plans overlap`

- **Usage**: `phax plans overlap [FLAGS] <plan>…`

Reports which of two or more plans can run in parallel without a merge conflict — predicted from each plan's declared file-sets, or confirmed against a landed run's actual diff.

(Predicted) Without --landed: reads each plan.md's structured form through the content-addressed extraction cache (a cold cache miss extracts once via LLM and caches the result; use --no-extract to fail on a miss instead). Unions each plan's declared phase file-sets into a per-plan footprint, intersects footprints pairwise, and reports the severity-graded conflict matrix, clean pairs, the largest fully-disjoint parallel-safe set, and a greedy wave schedule.

(Confirmed) With --landed <run>: takes a run that has already produced changes and reports which of the given plans need re-adjustment because they touch a file the run actually changed. The landed run's footprint is read from its persisted global-file-reconciliation.json (the real git diff across its phases), giving actual-vs-declared impact with no false negatives.

Caveats: the predicted mode reflects declared file intentions, not what agents will actually touch. Conflicts are file-level, not hunk-level — two plans editing different regions of the same file are flagged even if git would auto-merge them. Regenerated artifacts (phax.usage.kdl, docs/cli/reference.md) are a hard-conflict class.

Side effects: read-only with respect to your plans; may run one LLM extraction per uncached plan.md.

### Arguments

#### `<plan>…`

Paths to two or more plan.md files

### Flags

#### `--json`

Emit the overlap result as JSON instead of a report

#### `--no-extract`

Fail on a cache miss instead of extracting the plan.md

#### `--landed <run>`

Report which of the given plans need re-adjustment after this run's actual changes

### Examples

```
phax plans overlap docs/plans/2609101031-a-plan.md docs/plans/2609101032-b-plan.md
```

```
phax plans overlap --landed my-feature docs/plans/2609101033-other-plan.md
```

## `phax plans lint`

- **Usage**: `phax plans lint [--json] <plan>`

Reports every mechanical defect of a plan.md that phax can establish before a run, as findings with a severity (error or warning), a check, and the phase they concern.

Eight checks run: structure — every field the deterministic extraction requires, reported in full rather than stopping at the first; files — the planned create/edit lists walked in phase order against the working tree, so an edit of a file no earlier phase creates, a create of a file that already exists or was already created, and a phase that both creates and edits a path are errors (a path listed both to create and as optional is the one warning; optional files are never checked); commands — the plan's required commands against security.agentCommands and the gate profile; models — each phase's model and effort against the routing catalog, with alternatives when one is refused, each assignment bound of phax.json against the catalog, and each phase against the first bound that matches a file it plans to touch (or the policy default when none does): a departure without an **Assignment reason:** line is an error against a bound and a warning against the default, and a **Model reason:** line is an error (the label is now **Assignment reason:**); when a bound names an architecture part, the architecture provider runs once to resolve it; interactive and oracles — a malformed **Mode:** or oracle line is an error; so are the interactive-phase rules: an interactive phase that is the first or the last phase, one that directly follows another interactive phase, and one that plans a file to create or edit (its optional files name what the person may touch); and so are the oracle-phase rules: an **Oracle phase:** line without **Oracle files:** (or the reverse), a discharging phase that is not later in the plan or does not exist, a phase that is both an oracle phase and a discharging phase or discharges more than one oracle phase, an oracle file listed more than once on the **Oracle files:** line, an oracle file that is not a planned file of the oracle phase or that a phase in between plans, an interactive phase in a role (one between the pair is allowed), and an oracle phase when no oracles provider is configured (the provider is never spawned by lint); tests — a test line off the format is an error, one per phase naming its first departing line, and the other checks run on the plan without the departing lines; so are an oracle-loop line on a phase that is not an oracle phase, an oracle phase with no oracle-loop line (a phase with no test line at all included), and a criterion id the source spec's sidecar lacks; a criterion no line names is a warning, and so is a source spec whose criterion ids cannot be read (no sidecar, not found, a sidecar that does not read, or a source-spec that is not a spec path under docs/specs/, which is never read), in which case no criterion id is checked. The source spec's JSON sidecar is read in any shape, from docs/specs/archive/ when the spec has moved there; a plan with no source spec checks no criterion, and a loose plan.md whose frontmatter does not decode gets one warning naming the problem and checks no criterion. A phase with nothing to test is not flagged; advisory — when phax.json registers a planAuditor, phax writes the plan projection (the ordered phases, each with its planned create/edit files, and nothing else) to that command's stdin and reports every finding it returns as a warning naming the phases it concerns; a failing auditor is a single warning, and so is one that outruns the 30s cap phax spawns it under; with no auditor, or a plan the parser cannot read, there are no advisory findings. Advisory findings never affect the exit code.

A plan under docs/plans/ is first validated like any artifact (a name off <YYMMDDHHMM>-<slug>-plan.md, an invalid frontmatter block or a status/location disagreement refuses with exit code 12), and a slug that differs from its source spec's slug is a structure error; a loose plan.md outside docs/plans/ is exempt from both.

The file-plan ground is the working tree as it is now, not any commit. Read-only and model-free: it never writes, never reads the extraction cache and never falls back to the extraction model, so a plan the deterministic parser cannot read reports its structural errors and stops. Exits 1 when at least one finding is an error, 0 otherwise (warnings alone do not fail). An invalid config, a malformed bound or a user overlay that carries assignments included, exits 2.

Side effects: none of phax's own; a registered plan auditor is spawned once with the projection on stdin, capped at 30s.

### Arguments

#### `<plan>`

Path to the plan.md

### Flags

#### `--json`

Emit the findings as JSON

### Examples

```
phax plans lint docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md
```

```
phax plans lint docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md --json
```

## `phax plans overview`

- **Usage**: `phax plans overview [--json] <plan>`

Lays a plan out before it runs. For each phase in plan order it shows the model, effort and mode, the oracle role (an oracle phase and the phase that discharges it, or none), the planned files to create and edit grouped by architecture part, and the test lines. It ends with the coverage of the source spec's acceptance criteria: each criterion with the phases and loops whose test lines name it (`phase-02 in-phase ×2` when two lines of a phase and loop name it), then the criteria no line names. Cost is not shown; `phax plans estimate` keeps that.

The plan is read by the deterministic parser `phax plans lint` uses; no model reads it and no model session starts. It runs in any plan status, reads the plan and the source spec's JSON sidecar (from docs/specs/archive/ when the spec has moved there), and writes nothing. A plan under docs/plans/ is first validated like any artifact.

Parts: when phax.json registers an architecture provider, it runs once with the plan's planned files to create and edit (the whole repository when there are none). Each file is shown under every part whose globs match it, in the report's order, and the files no part holds are shown under (no part). Without a provider the planned files are shown as they are, and the header says so. A provider that fails or is refused is not an error: the overview degrades to the planned files, prints one line on stderr, `Warning: architecture provider failed: <message>`, and exits 0.

Coverage: a plan without a source spec prints no criterion coverage. A source spec with no JSON sidecar, one that is not found, a sidecar that does not read, or a source-spec that is not a spec path under docs/specs/ (never read) prints the one line `phax plans lint` reports for it, and no coverage. A loose plan.md whose frontmatter does not decode says so in its header and in that one line, and reads no source spec.

A plan the deterministic parser cannot read, including one with a test line off the format, prints one line on stderr naming the plan and `phax plans lint <plan>`, and exits 1: lint says what is wrong. A plan that fails artifact validation prints the plan and that validation error on one line and exits 1; a plan file that cannot be read prints the read failure and exits 1.

--json prints the overview as one JSON document on stdout, nothing else (warnings go to stderr). It carries the same content as the text: frontmatter.kind is decoded (with status), none or undecodable (with problem); architecture.kind is parts, none or failed; each phase has its oracleRole (oracle with dischargedBy, discharging with oraclePhase, or none), its placement (a list of { part, files } ending with the { part: null } entry of the unplaced files) and its testLines; coverage.kind is criteria (one entry per naming line), no-source-spec, frontmatter-undecodable or no-criterion-ids (with a reason). The document is unversioned, like `plans lint`'s.

Exit codes: 0 for an overview, a degraded architecture included; 1 for a plan that cannot be read, does not parse or fails artifact validation; 2 for an invalid phax.json.

Side effects: none of its own; the architecture provider is spawned once when one is configured.

### Arguments

#### `<plan>`

Path to the plan.md

### Flags

#### `--json`

Emit the overview as JSON

### Examples

```
phax plans overview docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md
```

```
phax plans overview docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md --json
```

## `phax plans estimate`

- **Usage**: `phax plans estimate [--json] [--no-probe] <plan>`

Estimate a plan's API-list cost and whether it fits the subscription windows now. Reports P10/P50/P90 in API-list dollars for each phase and for the run, then a verdict on the Claude subscription windows left right now.

History: the estimate is calibrated from this machine's cost ledgers. Only this repository's kept runs are sized (each phase by its planned-file bytes), and recent runs weigh more, with a half-life of 30 days. An estimate needs at least 60 sized phases; below that the verdict is thin-history and no estimate is printed. Every kept run with no ledger first gets one, as `phax cost backfill` writes it, and a line on stderr says how many were written; the report counts the kept runs still without one (a locked run is skipped).

Windows: by default, one minimal Claude Code probe on the cheapest Claude model reads the five-hour and seven-day windows from its rate-limit event. The probe gets a fixed prompt and never sees the plan; it spends one small request. --no-probe uses the last rate-limit sample in the cost ledgers instead, with no request; usage since that sample is not counted. phax never reads Claude Code's credentials or its OAuth usage endpoint. Each window's dollar capacity is recalibrated from the ledgers of the last 28 days.

Verdict: fits (no pause even at P90), risky (fits at P50, a pause is possible at P90), wait (a pause is expected at P50), thin-history (fewer than 60 sized phases), no-subscription (Claude Code authenticates with an API key), windows-unavailable (the windows could not be read; the reason is given) or uncalibrated (a window or the burn rate had no recent samples). An interactive phase is sized from its first and closing turns alone, from at least 3 past interactive phases with turn entries, repriced at its model and weighted by recency; it has its own row at its place in the plan, and mode: interactive in --json. A phase on a hold is part of a run, never sized. Never estimated: plan extraction, the plan auditor and the interactive code review; a phase routed to Codex or Mistral Vibe, or to a Claude model with no list price, is named and left out of the run total; the compliance review is named when it cannot be estimated.

The plan is read by the deterministic parser `phax plans lint` uses; no model reads it. A plan under docs/plans/ is first validated like any artifact. --json prints the report as one JSON document on stdout; warnings go to stderr.

Exit codes: 0 for any verdict; 1 for a plan the deterministic parser cannot read; 2 for an invalid phax.json, model-routing.json or providers.json; 10 for a corrupt run registry; 12 when the plan fails artifact validation.

Side effects: writes cost-ledger.json in each kept run folder that has none, as `phax cost backfill` does; without --no-probe, one Claude Code request.

### Arguments

#### `<plan>`

Path to the plan.md

### Flags

#### `--json`

Emit the estimate as JSON

#### `--no-probe`

Use the last rate-limit sample in the cost ledgers instead of a one-message Claude Code probe

### Examples

```
phax plans estimate docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md
```

```
phax plans estimate docs/plans/2609101200-foo-plan.md --no-probe --json
```

## `phax records`

- **Usage**: `phax records <SUBCOMMAND>`

Manage phax run records

## `phax records init`

- **Usage**: `phax records init [--force]`

Configure records for this project (transcript, destination, auto-push)

### Flags

#### `--force`

Reconfigure records even if already configured

## `phax records sync`

- **Usage**: `phax records sync`

Bring the local records clone in line with its configured remote

## `phax records status`

- **Usage**: `phax records status`

Show pending (unpushed) records, by run and phase

## `phax records list`

- **Usage**: `phax records list [--run <id>]`

List records present: phase records by run, phase, and verified surfaces; review entries by run and review; authoring and decision records by id and artifact

### Flags

#### `--run <id>`

Only show records for this run id

## `phax records explain`

- **Usage**: `phax records explain [FLAGS] <sha>`

Explains a commit from its record. The commit is a phase commit, a declared interactive phase's commit (Phase-Id with Interactive-Phase), or a held phase's review commit, which carries Run-Id and Held-Phase and resolves to the held phase's record. The output adds the stop's lines: its mode, cause, outcome, the person who closed it, the review commit, and each recorded session with its provider, model, origin and its transcript's sha256, or the reason it is missing. A stop's record never carries the transcript itself: interactive transcripts stay in the run folder whatever records.transcript says.

A run-level review entry's own commit on phax/records/v1 (Run-Id and Review trailers) is a record, not a source commit: explain names the run and the review and prints the git show that reads the review's file, and exits 0.

### Arguments

#### `<sha>`

Commit sha in the source repository (a phase commit or an artifact commit)

### Flags

#### `--prompt`

Print the full prompt

#### `--diff`

Print the full diff

#### `--transcript`

Print the full transcript

#### `--gates`

Print the gate check logs, each followed by its gate request

#### `--briefs`

Print the phase's brief records (brief-NN.json) in number order

### Examples

```
phax records explain 3f9c2a1
```

```
phax records explain 3f9c2a1 --gates
```
